title: Impact of Cooling Media on the Microstructure of AA6061 After High-Temperature Solution Treatment
content: Aluminum alloy 6061 (AA6061) is widely used due to its excellent weldability, corrosion resistance, and high strength-to-weight ratio. This alloy's principal constituents are aluminum, magnesium, and silicon, with minor iron, copper, chromium, and zinc additions. The microstructure, particularly the distribution and morphology of precipitates and dispersoids, is determined by the specific alloying elements and processing conditions [1]. Heat treatment is commonly employed to enhance mechanical properties, notably hardness and strength, primarily through the precipitation of the β-Mg2Si phase [2].
